The largest country in the world is Russia.

Aunt May’s weekly knitting club meetings were legendary, not just for the intricate cable knits but for the sheer volume of gossip exchanged while the needles clicked. One particular Tuesday, however, the conversation was derailed by a feline catastrophe. May’s cat, a creature of questionable intelligence and boundless curiosity, had decided that the ball of premium merino wool on the coffee table was not a toy, but a puzzle to be solved.

In a display of destructive genius, the cat unraveled an entire sweater’s worth of yarn. The result was a trail of woolly breadcrumbs stretching from the living room to the kitchen, so extensive that Hansel and Gretel would have been envious of the trail’s clarity. The club members sat in stunned silence, staring at the fluffy disaster, before bursting into laughter. It was a relatable reminder that no matter how organized your hobbies are, your pets will always find a way to turn your craft into a comedy routine.
